newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures tradeless waiting on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures tradeless waiting on USDA report.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures failed to trade again on Friday as the market waited on the USDA crop report due on Monday.
Most settlement prices firmed slightly, by 50 cents to A$2.00 a tonne, although nearby May slipped by 50 cents.
"Most people are waiting to see what the USDA report says. The market is taking a 'wait and see' attitude," Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said.
The USDA crop report, believed to be bullish for prices, had been mostly factored in, while further information on U.S. crop progress and freeze damage was expected soon, he said.
The market has become comfortable with some U.S. damage but could be surprised by the amount of damage, he said.

Provided the market did not break through US$3.98 a bushel it should hold, he said. "We now expect the market will try to move higher and may move quickly higher on a more accurate assessment of U.S. freeze damage," he said.
Patchy rain in Australia's eastern states left a strong need for follow-up rain for this season's planting, he said.
Much hedge activity remained to be done at A$190.00 and higher for January 1998, but at present levels around A$180.00 there was very little interest from either side, he said.
